'''Luke Douglas Kennard''' ({{IPAc-en|k|ə|ˈ|n|ɑːr|d}} {{respell|kə|NARD}};<ref>{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> born June 24, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils]] and was drafted by the [[Detroit Pistons]] with the 12th pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. He has also played for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], and [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. His .4421 [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] [[field goal percentage]] currently ranks [[List of NBA career 3-point field goal percentage leaders|second in NBA history]] and first amongst active players.{{efn|Minimum 250 career three-point field goals made.}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=NBA & ABA Career Leaders and Records for 3-Pt Field Goal Pct|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leaders/fg3_pct_career.html|access-date=December 21, 2024|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref>

==High school career==
Kennard attended [[Franklin High School (Franklin, Ohio)|Franklin High School]] in [[Franklin, Ohio]] near [[Dayton, Ohio|Dayton]]. As a senior, he was named the ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'' National Player of the Year. He was named the Ohio [[Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year]] as junior and senior. He also played high school football, lettering for three years as a quarterback. And though he shot with his left hand in basketball, he threw with his right hand in football.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Duke men's basketball 2016–17 player review: Luke Kennard|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2017/03/duke-mens-basketball-2016-17-player-review-luke-kennard|access-date=2020-12-24|website=The Chronicle}}</ref>

Finishing high school, Kennard was one of the most sought after recruits in the nation.<ref>[http://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2014/03/21/franklins-luke-kennard-gatorade-ohio-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/6697743/ Franklin's Luke Kennard named Gatorade Player of the Year]</ref><ref>[http://www.cincinnati.com/story/blogs/2015/03/19/luke-kennard-named-gatorade-ohio-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/25010547/ Luke Kennard named Gatorade Ohio Player of the Year]</ref> He was ranked as the No. 24 prospect in his recruiting class by [[ESPN]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=2015 guard Luke Kennard commits to Duke basketball|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2014/03/2015-guard-luke-kennard-commits-duke-basketball|access-date=2020-12-24|website=The Chronicle}}</ref> Kennard committed to [[Duke University]] to play college basketball during his junior year of high school.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Duke basketball 2015–16 player preview: Luke Kennard|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2015/11/151103-mbb-preview-kennard|access-date=2020-12-24|website=The Chronicle}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/10668122 Luke Kennard commits to Duke]</ref><ref>[http://www.courier-journal.com/story/recruiting/2014/03/24/kennard-commits-to-duke/6847269/ Luke Kennard commits to Duke]</ref> He finished his career with the second most points in Ohio history, three spots ahead of [[LeBron James]].<ref name=":0"/><ref>[http://usatodayhss.com/2015/no-18-franklin-falls-luke-kennard-finishes-no-2-in-scoring-in-ohio-history No. 18 Franklin falls; Luke Kennard finishes No. 2 in scoring in Ohio history]</ref> He was a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] selection.<ref name=":1"/>

In 2020, it was announced that Franklin High would retire Kennard's number 10.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Richter|first=Ed|date=28 October 2020|title=Franklin honoring all-time great Luke Kennard with number retirement|work=Dayton Daily News}}</ref>

==College career==
===Freshman season (2015–2016)===
In practice, he frequently matched up against Duke guard [[Grayson Allen]].<ref name=":1"/>

On January 6, 2016, Luke scored 23 points in a 91–75 win over [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400839276|title=Allen, Plumlee lead No.14 Duke past Wake Forest, 91–75|date=January 6, 2016|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=January 7, 2016}}</ref> On February 6, 2016, Kennard tallied 26 points in an 88–80 win over [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400839770|title=Allen, Kennard lead Duke past NC State, 88–80|date=February 6, 2016|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=February 6, 2016}}</ref> As a freshman at Duke, Kennard averaged 11.8 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.5 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=R.|last=Cassano|title=Franklin’s Kennard elevating his game with Blue Devils|url=http://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/franklin-kennard-elevating-his-game-with-blue-devils/0sIboGc0oemtPicuC66ksM/|work=Dayton Daily News|date=December 16, 2016|access-date=November 22, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=C.L.|last=Brown|title=Luke Kennard has been one of few sure things for Duke|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18452498|website=ESPN.com|date=January 26, 2017|access-date=November 22, 2021}}</ref>

===Sophomore season (2016–2017)===
On November 29, 2016, Kennard scored 20 points in a 78–69 win against [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] in [[ACC–Big Ten Challenge]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400915066|title=Allen leads No.5 Duke past Michigan State 78–69|date=November 29, 2016|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=November 30, 2016}}</ref> On December 3, 2016, Kennard scored 35 points in a 94–55 win over Maine.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400915281|title=No.5 Duke beats Maine 94–55 without 2 starting guards|date=December 3, 2016|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=December 5, 2017}}</ref> On January 28, 2017, Kennard scored 34 points in an 85–83 win over [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://goduke.com/news/2017/1/28/211440494.aspx|title=Kennard Sinks WF with Late 3, Scores 34 in 85–83 Win|date=January 28, 2017|publisher=Duke Athletics|access-date=February 6, 2017}}</ref> On February 11, 2017, Kennard tallied 25 points in a 64–62 victory over [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400915434|title=Kennard, No.18 Duke hold on to beat Clemson 64–62|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=February 11, 2017}}</ref> On March 3, 2017, Luke scored 20 points in a 79–72 victory over [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] in the second round <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://goduke.com/news/2017/3/8/211516351.aspx|title=Tatum, Kennard, Jackson Each score 20 in 79–72 Win|publisher=Duke Athletics|date=March 3, 2017|access-date=March 3, 2017}}</ref> and scored 24 points in an 81–77 win against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] in the quarterfinals of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|2017 ACC tournament]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400945793|title=Tatum, Allen lead Duke comeback vs Louisville, 81–77|date=March 9, 2017|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=March 9, 2017}}</ref> On March 10, 2017, Kennard scored 20 points in a 93–83 win over rival [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] in the semifinals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400946137|title=No.14 Duke races past No.6 UNC 93–83 in ACC semifinals|date=March 10, 2017|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=March 11, 2017}}</ref> On March 11, 2017, Kennard tallied 16 points in a 75–69 win against [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] in the ACC Championship game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400946221|title=Duke downs Notre Dame to become first 4–in–4 ACC champion|date=March 11, 2017|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=March 11, 2017}}</ref>

During his sophomore year, Luke averaged 19.5 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game. He led the team both from the three-point range with 43.8% and free throw line at 85.6%. As a sophomore, he was named first team All-ACC and second-team All-American.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2017/3/5/58bc7714e4b0af375f7cb2ea_131480910878223641.aspx?path=mbball|title=ACC Announces All-Conference Team, Postseason Awards|website=theacc.com|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=March 5, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Duke men's basketball 2016–17 player review: Luke Kennard|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2017/03/duke-mens-basketball-2016-17-player-review-luke-kennard|access-date=2020-12-24|website=The Chronicle}}</ref>

He finished 1–6 from the field and fouled out in Duke's second-round loss to [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] in the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=SOUTH CAROLINA STUNNER: Gamecocks overwhelm Duke men's basketball in Round of 32 upset|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2017/03/south-carolina-stunner-gamecocks-overwhelm-duke-mens-basketball-in-round-of-32-upset|access-date=2020-12-24|website=The Chronicle}}</ref> His reaction to the final foul call against him quickly turned into a meme.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Internet Can't Stop Laughing at This March Madness Meme|url=https://time.com/4706903/march-madness-2017-duke-luke-kennard-meme/|access-date=2020-12-24|website=Time}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Baumann|first=Michael|date=2017-03-20|title=For One Night, South Carolina Basketball Is the Toast of the Nation|url=https://www.theringer.com/2017/3/20/16043334/2017-ncaa-tournament-south-carolina-duke-3afe19b61af6|access-date=2020-12-24|website=The Ringer|language=en}}</ref>

After his sophomore season, Kennard chose to forgo his final two years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/acc/2017/04/06/duke-guard-luke-kennard-declares-nba-draft-hires-agent/100131302/|title=Duke's Luke Kennard declares for NBA draft, hires an agent|website=USA Today|author=Gleeson|date=April 6, 2017|access-date=April 6, 2017|first=Scott}}</ref> He joined Duke teammates [[Jayson Tatum]], [[Harry Giles (basketball)|Harry Giles]], and [[Frank Jackson (basketball)|Frank Jackson]] in declaring early for the draft.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Luke Kennard declares for NBA Draft after standout sophomore campaign|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2017/04/luke-kennard-declares-for-nba-draft-after-standout-sophomore-campaign|access-date=2020-12-24|website=The Chronicle}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Detroit Pistons (2017–2020)===
[[File:Luke Kennard - Pistons vs. Pacers Oct 23 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Kennard with the Detroit Pistons in 2019]]
On June 22, 2017, Kennard was drafted 12th overall by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2017 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2017/06/23/detroit-pistons-2017-nba-draft/421684001/|title=Pistons take Duke's Luke Kennard with 12th overall pick in 2017 NBA draft|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|first=Vince|last=Ellis|date=June 22, 2017|access-date=June 22, 2017}}</ref>

He made his NBA debut on October 20, 2017, against the [[Washington Wizards]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.journal-news.com/sports/luke-kennard-scores-double-figures-nba-debut/EW6o72RdP4jbWMW6a4GySO/|title=Luke Kennard scores in double figures in NBA debut|work=journal-news|access-date=September 15, 2018}}</ref> scoring 11 points and recording 2 [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] in 18 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201710200WAS.html|title=Detroit Pistons at Washington Wizards Box Score, October 20, 2017|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=September 15, 2018}}</ref> Kennard started his first NBA game on December 15, 2017, after [[Avery Bradley]] suffered a groin injury, scoring 9 points with 5 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 4 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] in a win against the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-luke-kennard-starting-at-shooting-guard-friday/|title=Pistons' Luke Kennard: Starting at shooting guard Friday|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=September 15, 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201712150IND.html|title=Detroit Pistons at Indiana Pacers Box Score, December 15, 2017|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=September 15, 2018}}</ref> Kennard recorded his first career [[Double (basketball)|double-double]] on January 24, 2018, with 10 points and 10 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fantasypros.com/nba/news/147105/luke-kennard-posts-first-career-double-double-ot-loss-to-jazz.php|title=Luke Kennard posts first career double-double in OT loss to Jazz|date=January 25, 2018|work=FantasyPros|access-date=September 15, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201801240DET.html|title=Utah Jazz at Detroit Pistons Box Score, January 24, 2018|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=September 15, 2018}}</ref> On April 11, 2018, Kennard recorded a former career-high 23 points in a 119–87 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2018/08/role_of_pistons_luke_kennard_c.html|title=Role of Pistons' Luke Kennard could expand under Dwane Casey|work=MLive.com|access-date=September 15, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

In July 2018, the Pistons announced that Kennard suffered a left knee [[Strain (injury)|strain]] and would miss the 2018 NBA Summer League.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2729861-pistons-luke-kennard-out-for-rest-of-nba-summer-league-due-to-knee-injury|title=Pistons' Luke Kennard out for Rest of NBA Summer League Due to Knee Injury|last=Zucker|first=Joseph|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=September 15, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> On October 26, 2018, Kennard suffered a sprain of the AC joint in his right shoulder and would be out for at least two weeks. On December 10, 2018, he recorded a career-high 28 points in a 116–102 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. On April 10, 2019, Kennard recorded 27 points in the last game of the regular season, in a 115–89 win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/10/25/kennard-leaves-game-shoulder-injury|title=Pistons' Kennard diagnosed with right shoulder sprain|date=October 26, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 26, 2018}}</ref>

On October 23, 2019, Kennard scored 30 points and three rebounds in a 119–110 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160626|title=Andre Drummond helps Pistons beat Pacers in opener|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 23, 2019|date=October 23, 2019|agency=The Associated Press}}</ref> The season was Kennard's first as a full-time starter for the Pistons, but it was cut short after 28 games due to bilateral knee tendinitis and, subsequently, the suspension of the season due to COVID-19.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Sankofa|first=Omari II|title=After injury, Luke Kennard is in the 'best shape' of his career, playing more point guard|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2020/09/25/detroit-pistons-luke-kennard/3525453001/|access-date=2020-12-24|website=Detroit Free Press|language=en-US|date=2020-09-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Sankofa|first=Omari II|title=Now 100% healthy, Detroit Pistons' Luke Kennard has big goals for next season|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2020/06/13/detroit-pistons-luke-kennard-health/3179462001/|access-date=2020-12-24|website=Detroit Free Press|language=en-US|date=2020-06-13}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2020–2023)===
[[File:Luke Kennard - 51849060280 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|Kennard with the Los Angeles Clippers in 2022]]
On November 19, 2020, Kennard was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in a three-team trade that involved the [[Brooklyn Nets]], sending [[Rodney McGruder]], [[Džanan Musa]] and the draft rights of [[Saddiq Bey]] and [[Jaylen Hands]] to Detroit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-acquire-kennard-patton-scrubb-and-four-second-round-picks-three-team-deal|title=LA Clippers Acquire Kennard, Patton, Scrubb and Four Second-Round Picks In Three-Team Deal|work=NBA.com|date=November 19, 2020}}</ref> On December 21, 2020, Kennard signed a four-year, $64 million extension through the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 21, 2020 |title=LA Clippers, Luke Kennard reach 4-year, $64 million extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30574961 |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski}}</ref> On March 22, 2021, Kennard posted 20 points on 8-for-8 from the field, including 4-for-4 from 3-point range coming off the bench, along with seven rebounds, four assists and a block in 18 minutes of action in a 119–110 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]], becoming the first player in franchise history to log at least 20 points, seven rebounds and four assists with less than 20 minutes of playing time in a game.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Clippers' Luke Kennard: Helps to spur huge comeback|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-luke-kennard-helps-to-spur-huge-comeback/|access-date=2021-03-24|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-03-23|title=Luke Kennard showing Clippers he deserves shot to play more|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/story/2021-03-23/luke-kennard-clippers-play-more|access-date=2021-03-24|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US}}</ref>

On December 18, 2021, Kennard scored a season-high 27 points, alongside seven rebounds and three assists, in a 104–103 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER HITS 3 AT BUZZER, THUNDER BEAT CLIPPERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100444 |access-date=March 14, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 25, 2022, he was fouled while shooting a three-pointer and made the shot as well as the free throw, which propelled the Clippers to a 116–115 win over the [[Washington Wizards]]. The Clippers had trailed by as many as 35 points during the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=KENNARD SCORES 7 IN FINAL 9 SECONDS AS CLIPPERS STUN WIZARDS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100716 |access-date=March 14, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Kennard missed the Clippers’ two postseason [[NBA Play-In Tournament|play-in tournament]] games with a hamstring injury,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-16 |title=Clippers' Luke Kennard: Out Friday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-luke-kennard-out-friday/ |access-date=2026-07-01 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref> as they were eliminated from playoff contention for the first time since [[2018 NBA playoffs|2018]].

===Memphis Grizzlies (2023–2025)===
On February 9, 2023, Kennard was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Luke Kennard in three-team trade|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-acquire-luke-kennard-in-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}}</ref> He made his Grizzlies debut three days later, recording four points and two rebounds in a 119–109 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=WHITE'S 23 POINTS HELPS CELTICS PAST GRIZZLIES 119–109|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200855|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 14, 2023}}</ref> On March 24, Kennard scored a career-high-tying 30 points in a 151–114 win over the [[Houston Rockets]]. His ten made 3-pointers set a Grizzlies franchise record for most threes made in a game, surpassing the previous mark (9) set twice by [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]] and once by teammate [[Jaren Jackson Jr.]]<ref>{{cite web|title=GRIZZLIES CLINCH PLAYOFF BERTH WITH 151–114 ROUT OF ROCKETS|url=https://www.nba.com/game/hou-vs-mem-0022201100|website=NBA.com|access-date=March 24, 2023}}</ref>

On July 31, 2024, Kennard re-signed with the Grizzlies on a one-year, $9.25 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies re-sign Luke Kennard|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-re-sign-luke-kennard|website=NBA.com|date=July 31, 2024|access-date=August 1, 2024}}</ref> He made 65 appearances (11 starts) for Memphis in the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 8.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 3.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Luke Kennard 2024–25 Game Log|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3913174/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2025–2026)===
On July 8, 2025, Kennard signed a one-year, $11 million contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Guard Luke Kennard|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-guard-luke-kennard|website=NBA.com|date=Jul 8, 2025|access-date=Jul 8, 2025}}</ref> Kennard made 46 appearances off of the bench for Atlanta during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 7.9 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 2.1 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Luke Kennard 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3913174/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2026)===
On February 5, 2026, Kennard was traded by the Hawks to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Gabe Vincent]] and a future second-round pick.<ref>{{cite On July 14, 2026, Kennard signed a two-year, $12.4 million contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-guard-luke-kennard|title=Suns Sign Guard Luke Kennard|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2026}}</ref>

In 2017, Kennard briefly dated television personality [[Savannah Chrisley (influencer)|Savannah Chrisley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2017/12/27/savannah-chrisleys-nba-ex-rebounds-with-former-flame/|title=Savannah Chrisley’s NBA ex rebounds with former flame|last=Hendricks|first=Jaclyn|date=December 27, 2017|website=[[The New York Post]]|access-date=April 15, 2026}}</ref> Kennard and long-time girlfriend Anna Castro were married on August 5, 2022.
